agent.summary: xs-rs now packs small DATA records across directory NEEDs instead of flushing one tiny DATA frame per NEED, and automatic compression no longer spends zstd on kilobyte-sized listings. On a 2-CPU, 11 ms-RTT race of the congress-sample update-10pct shape it improved from 1.61 s to 1.43 s against the parent binary, with CPU down about 13%. Explicit -z still compresses every listing as before.
agent.diagnosis: On a local fakessh pipe xs-rs was already faster, so I reproduced the lab shape with two-CPU affinity and an 11 ms relay. The update path was sending roughly one DATA frame per NEED (about 2,500 DATA frames for ~20 MiB of changed data) because each worker flushed its block at the end of every read task, even when the task held one small file. Under the same latency, auto-compression also spent zstd frames on nearly 10,000 small DIR listings. The parent measured 1.61 s wall / 0.63 s CPU with the lab update shape; the candidate 1.43 s / 0.55 s.
agent.change: In rs/xs-rs/src/transfer.rs, workers now keep a partial DATA block across NEEDs and flush it at 256 KiB, at a skip-compress boundary, or when the worker has no more reads. DATA_END is emitted by the last worker after every worker has flushed, so no DATA can follow it. Automatic compression now compresses a DIR body only when it is at least 16 KiB; explicit -z still compresses all listings as xs-c++ does. Added a workers.rs regression test for 300 one-file directories plus a changed second pass.
agent.expected_effect: Fewer DATA frames and fewer per-frame checksums, queue operations and writes on update-heavy trees, plus less CPU on small listings. In the local lab-shaped A/B this was 0.88x-0.91x the parent wall time and about 13% less CPU.
agent.risks: Batching can delay a partial DATA block by up to 256 KiB per worker, and DATA_END now depends on all workers reporting their flush; this ordering is covered by the new test and the existing interop suite. Skipping automatic compression of small listings trades a little wire size for CPU; -z and explicitly requested compression are unchanged, and frames remain wire-compatible.
